traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's western swordfern review (Zouhar 2015, read 2026-10-15): frond size varies with place and site, from about 8 to 98 inches (20-250 cm) long; fronds over 3 feet (1 m) typify the fern where it dominates the understory. The stated 25 cm to 1 m is the common part of that range.

traits.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon): a stout, ascending rhizome; fronds 30 to 140 cm, rigidly ascending in a crown, evergreen and leathery; stipes 5 to 60 cm; blades linear-lanceolate, 25 to 100 cm by 5 to 25 cm, once pinnate, the pinnae many, narrow, sharply double-toothed; sori large, in one row halfway to the margin or nearer it, sometimes in several crowded rows.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a large evergreen fern: a fountain of stiff, arching, once-divided fronds. Not fitted to measurements. Its angles, droop, pinna count and pinna sizes along the blade are the fern rules', from its stated posture, blade shape and measures.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.8 m tall at 8 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark glossy green fronds.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.indusium.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 460, 461, Polystichum munitum: indusium shield, ciliate.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America (vol. 2), Polystichum munitum: "Petiole 1/8--1/4 length of leaf". Of Abrams's blades 25 to 100 cm, that is a stipe a seventh to a third as long as the blade, 4 to 33 cm; Abrams's "stipes 5 to 60 cm" is kept as the rare high.

traits.stipe_scales.note: Flora of North America (vol. 2), Polystichum munitum: "Petiole ... densely scaly; scales red-brown to dark brown or nearly black, gradually diminishing in size distally."

traits.stipe_scale_colour.note: Flora of North America's "red-brown to dark brown or nearly black" scales (see stipe_scales), read as a dark red-brown.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon), Polystichum munitum: fronds "rigidly ascending in a crown"; read as ascending.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: The spec's value is from its `traits` note (abrams-1923). Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 460-461: rhizome ascending to erect. The spec stated "ascending". Combined on the owner's rule (2026-10-15): where two sources differ, both are kept and the range spans them.
